cues.text: Simulated model, assumed signs. The takeoff replays recorded flight kinematics; the looming stimulus is our assumption — we activate LC4 and LPLC2 looming detectors.
Simulated model: the assumed looming input fires in the lobula and lobula plate, where LC4 and LPLC2 dendrites sample the scene.
Simulated model: the visual alarm collects in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum, the glomerulus zone where looming projection neurons terminate.
Simulated model: the signal funnels through the wedge and clamp toward descending neurons — our assumed giant-fiber escape relay.
Simulated model: the compass neuropils barely change — the assumed visual alarm bypasses them entirely.
Simulated model: the replayed wings buzz on; every spike stays simulated, built on assumed input and assumed cell signs.
Simulated model: the looming drive fades as the assumed threat passes; residual simulated activity washes out.

qa.q: What triggers escape in the model?
qa.a: An assumed looming stimulus on LC4 and LPLC2 visual projection neurons — a plausible threat input, not a published Shiu experiment.
The body motion is a reference replay of flight kinematics; all brain spikes are simulated.
A fast descending pathway driving jump-and-fly escapes. We mention it for context — our stimulus is an assumption on its upstream detectors.

qa.q: Why does it say assumed signs?
qa.a: The model guesses whether each synapse excites or inhibits from predicted transmitters. Guesses can be wrong, so we label them.
